newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts split on Trelleborg spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Analysts split on Trelleborg spin-off.

text.p: Analysts were mixed on Thursday on Swedish mining and rubber company Trelleborg AB's decision to spin off mining unit Boliden and list it in Toronto, Canada.
Speculation about such a move had driven the Trelleborg share price up in recent weeks.
At the close on Thursday Trelleborg shares were three crowns lwoer at 116.5 crowns.
Carnegie analyst Christofer Sjogren said Boliden's value was not fully realised while it was part of Trelleborg.

"I believe it can be difficult to determine what this means for Trelleborg given current information...I think it's positive and the borse will trade the Trelleborg share up ahead of Boliden's listing," said Sjogren.
Sjogren added he expected zinc prices to increase in the spring, which would make Boliden more valuable.
"I believe Trelleborg will fall on this. Boliden will probably be valued at around six billion crowns and this is in a positive scenario," one analyst said.
He said Trelleborg's plan to sell around 50 percent of Boliden would mean the company was giving up cash flow in exchange for parts of Boliden's result.
"Trelleborg is exchanging cash flow for shares in their profits, something that will increase the company's image as a conglomerate," one analyst said.
Analysts said they were now looking at what Trelleborg would do with the money from the sale.
"The value of Trelleborg is not bad at the moment. I would definitely not go after Trelleborg in the period before they announce what they'll do with the money," one said.

"They will have a great profit in 1997 and huge coffers of money that they must do something with. They will probably go in harder in their rubbers division which can not be valued especially high," one analyst said.
